newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury current sales rise, profits down.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury current sales rise, profits down.

text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc said on Wednesday that same store sales since the start of the current financial year were up 4.2 percent with total sales up 8.4 percent.

It said total sales in the 52 weeks ending March 8 were up six percent to 14.3 billion pounds ($23.4 billion) with pre-tax profits before exceptional charges at 651 million pounds, down 14.8 percent, as indicated by the company in January.

Chairman David Sainsbury said that higher costs and a petrol price war had hit the year's profits but added that "in the year ahead we are focused on sustaining higher sales momentum and translating this into satisfactory profit growth."

Sainsbury, which has been struggling to gain ground against market leader Tesco, said it aimed for "significant improvement" in operating profits from its Homebase do-it-yourself business and Shaw's in the U.S. after heavy investment.
The company said in its supermarkets business, there would be further developments in quality and choice, along with enhancements to value for money but that further costs should be limited.

Sainsbury said gross margins, excluding petrol, remained stable as higher petrol margins were offset by loyalty card and depreciation costs, but added that it hoped to increase "significantly" return on capital employed and earnings per share "in the medium term."
